candidate_relations.reason: The initial 2015 biopsy showed hepatic adenoma, but the reference diagnosis is choriocarcinoma. The two entities are incompatible: choriocarcinoma is a malignant trophoblastic neoplasm, whereas hepatic adenoma is a benign hepatocellular lesion. The evolving clinical picture (central necrosis, atypical HCC features, male sex, elevated suspicion prompting resection) points away from adenoma toward choriocarcinoma. C001 represents the superseded prior diagnosis, not the final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hepatic adenoma was the prior biopsy diagnosis; the reference diagnosis is choriocarcinoma, a distinct malignant germ-cell/trophoblastic tumor that the clinical course (hypervascular lesions with central necrosis, atypical imaging, bleeding, male patient on anticoagulation) ultimately revealed

case_quality_flags: serum hCG was not measured despite clinical suspicion for trophoblastic tumor in a male patient — a notable diagnostic gap
prior biopsy diagnosis of adenoma may represent sampling error or misclassification of choriocarcinoma
